newsitem.title: USA: US money managers hold bond durations steady -- MCM.
newsitem.headline: US money managers hold bond durations steady -- MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers held their dollar-weighted durations on their debt portfolios steady, an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey said.
"Cash positions fell further ... this nears the lows of early this year," said MCM MoneyWatch vice president Astrid Adolfson, who conducts the weekly survey.
More portfolio managers put cash to work, as the next likely move "sell" category rose further, Adolfson said.
The number of underweights in government debt fell, while the mortgage underweightings rose, according to the survey.
The survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark held steady at 108.1 percent in the week ending June 23.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 32 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," unchanged from the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 19 percent from 16 percent the week before.
Forty-nine percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.84 percent from 2.92 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 31 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, unchanged from the previous week, while 8.0 percent underweighted it. The remaining 61 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 52 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 11 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
